newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods likely to hurt Polish growth, CPI - c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Floods likely to hurt Polish growth, CPI - c.banker.

text.p: Poland's heavy flooding is likely to result in lower than expected growth this year and may boost inflation beyond earlier targets, the National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Thursday.
The flood so far has claimed 46 lives and water has swamped 4,500 sq km (1,700 square miles), of which around two-fifths was still inundated. It has struck 40,000 farms, 86 towns and 875 villages.
"The flood will have to affect the GDP (gross domestic product), we do not know yet on what scale. It can be half a point or a point, we do not know for now," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.

"It can also have an impact on inflation because of an increased deficit financing by the NBP (National Bank of Poland) but we will have to wait for July and August figures to see what will be its effect, for example, on food prices," she said.

The 1997 budget assumed a 5.5 percent GDP growth and a drop in year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December from 18.5 percent at the end of 1996. But recent government predictions were more optimistic, putting growth at about six percent and revising down the inflation target to 12 percent. @
Gronkiewicz-Waltz said, however, that a loss in output was inescapable despite an expected reconstruction boom.

Year-on-year inflation was expected to recede in July and August after a brief seasonal surge to 15.3 percent last month on a jump in food prices. Government officials have said the flood's impact on food prices would be minimal.
But Gronkiewicz-Waltz said crop losses might still result in a smaller than usual dip in food prices in summer months. @

She also said the extra 2.5 billion-zloty central bank financing limit granted the government by parliament to help it deal with the flood damage created an additional inflationary impulse. -- Tomasz Janowski +48 22 653 9700
